body.en: *Cytokinins* have specific effects on cytokinesis. Kinetin, a modified form of adenine, was discovered from autoclaved herring sperm DNA; it does not occur naturally in plants. Natural cytokinins, such as zeatin, were isolated from corn kernels and coconut milk. They are made in regions of rapid cell division: root apices, developing shoot buds and young fruits. Cytokinins help produce new leaves, chloroplasts in leaves, lateral shoot growth and adventitious shoot formation. They help overcome apical dominance, and they promote nutrient mobilisation, which delays leaf senescence.

narration.en: A ripening fruit makes ethylene, and ethylene makes it ripen faster and make more ethylene: the climacteric rise. A ripe fruit in the bag adds ethylene and speeds ripening; ventilation removes it; cold storage slows every step. This is why mangoes and bananas are ripened with ethylene (from ethephon) and stored cool.

say.en: Cytokinins promote cell division. They help new shoots and chloroplasts form, let lateral buds grow and delay leaf senescence.
Ethylene is a gas. It ripens fruits, causes senescence and abscission, breaks dormancy and makes deep-water rice internodes elongate.
Abscisic acid is the stress hormone. It closes stomata, keeps seeds dormant and opposes gibberellins.
During ripening, many fruits show a sudden burst of respiration, the climacteric. Ethylene triggers it.
Plant hormones act together. ABA and gibberellins are antagonists: one keeps seeds dormant, the other makes them germinate.

say.en: Sort the effects of three plant growth regulators.

body.en: *Ethylene* is a simple gaseous PGR synthesised in large amounts by tissues undergoing senescence and by ripening fruits. It influences horizontal growth of seedlings, swelling of the axis and apical hook formation in dicot seedlings. It promotes senescence and abscission, especially of leaves and flowers, and is highly effective in fruit ripening, raising the rate of respiration during ripening (respiratory climacteric). It breaks seed and bud dormancy, initiates germination in peanut seeds and sprouting of potato tubers, promotes rapid internode and petiole elongation in deep-water rice, and promotes root growth and root hair formation. It is used to initiate flowering and synchronise fruit set in pineapples and to induce flowering in mango. The most widely used source is ethephon, which in aqueous solution is readily absorbed and releases ethylene slowly; it hastens ripening in tomatoes and apples, accelerates abscission in flowers and fruits (thinning of cotton, cherry, walnut) and promotes female flowers in cucumbers. Ethylene is the most widely used PGR in agriculture.

points.en: Ethephon: ripening, thinning, female flowers in cucumber.

body.en: ABA was discovered for its role in regulating abscission and dormancy, but it has other wide-ranging effects. It acts as a general plant growth inhibitor and an inhibitor of plant metabolism. It inhibits seed germination. It stimulates the closure of stomata and increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stress; it is therefore also called the stress hormone. It plays an important role in seed development, maturation and dormancy; by inducing dormancy it helps seeds withstand desiccation and other unfavourable factors. In most situations ABA acts as an antagonist to gibberellins.

Column I: a Auxin b Gibberellin c Cytokinin d Abscisic acid
Column II: i Apical dominance ii Bolting in cabbage iii Delay of leaf senescence iv Closure of stomata.
Auxin from the apex causes apical dominance; gibberellins cause bolting in cabbage and beet; cytokinins delay leaf senescence; ABA closes stomata under stress.
